hypotheses.title: A narrowed workflow_dispatch satisfies 10 of the 13 release gates
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE: the runs API object the gate receives has no dispatch-input field, so a fixture cannot express the difference
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Add a selection marker (mode/all, probes/full) to each gate's release-evidence.json and a requiredEvidence rail that asserts the full selection; the planted-defect test is a fixture whose evidence says mode=assets and a manifest that requires all.
hypotheses.counterargument: A release manager is expected to dispatch the full selection, and the 4 gates without narrowing inputs (whole-session, worldinfo, helper-state, combination-journey) are full by construction; longlived already solved this with a tier marker. The gap is real only because the same remedy was not applied to CI and Browser differential.

hypotheses.title: The smoke-metrics release gate cannot fail on a performance regression
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE for the claim: run the gate with a doubled latency in the artifact; only the cold-start ceiling and structural properties are asserted
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Mutate a recorded metric x2 and re-run; if green, derive a per-metric tolerance from same-runner noise, add it to the asserted list, and show a planted x2 regression red.
hypotheses.counterargument: The single-sided job does assert a cold-start ceiling (60 s, ~30x measured), so a hang is caught; and the release bar's performance claim is regenerated from the recorded artifact rather than asserted, which is a deliberate reporting design. But the gate's green still reads as 'performance qualified' in the evidence table.

hypotheses.title: The combination-journey leg-failure counter is written and never consumed
hypotheses.reproducer: A leg that exits non-zero after writing a syntactically valid report whose steps are all ok: the job stays green; no assertion names it
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Add the missing step 'if steps.legs.outputs.failures != 0 -> exit 1' (the whole-session shape) and demonstrate it with a leg script that exits 3 after a green report.
hypotheses.counterargument: The comparator catches the common consequences: a missing report makes read() throw, and a leg with a not-ok step fails both-legs-have-no-failed-step. Only the 'failed after a good report' corner is invisible.

hypotheses.title: The 20-extension corpus can be green without executing extension code
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE yet: no case serves the assets without running the modules
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: A negative control case that serves the 20 manifests from a static tree while the extension scripts 404 or no-op; today the comparator would report the same set/status/state on both subjects and pass. Then add a per-extension behavioural marker (a slash command, a DOM node, an injected prompt) and require it on both subjects.
hypotheses.counterargument: The lifecycle shard job drives each extension's own setting and a real restart, so code execution is implied there; the all-20 job answers a different question (coexistence/load). But plan section 8 names 'actual extension code executed' as the evidence bar for the combined gate, and E04 is the combination.

hypotheses.title: 83 combination-journey guards, 5 demonstrated mutations, and the world-info-slot guard is explicitly undemonstrated
hypotheses.reproducer: Take a green pair and drop one world-info slot marker: if turn-1-world-info-three-slots-placed does not fire, the teeth for the E03 claim do not exist; if it is already red on a green pair, the gate cannot be green at all
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Run the existing probe on both subjects, save the pair, mutate the slot marker in memory and require the named red (the selftest pattern). The comment at :66-70 says the pair used while writing it had the pinned side already red, which must be re-measured.
hypotheses.counterargument: A mutation can only be demonstrated on a guard that is green in the baseline; the file says so and refuses to fake it. The deferred mutation is honest, not hidden, and docs/combination-journey.md records it. But the release gate still rests on a guard whose teeth were never observed.

hypotheses.title: There is no 120+ prompt preset on the browser side, so E03's stress profile cannot be met as specified
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE: the fixture does not exist; count prompts in every committed preset and in the generated corpus (105, 119, <=66, 120 only in Go)
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Generate the stress profile deterministically in a generator (tools/alpha16/scenario-preset.mjs or an extension of build-longlived-corpus.mjs), record its prompt count and sha256 in the report, and assert >=120 prompts and >=115 prompt_order rows in the scenario comparator.
hypotheses.counterargument: preset-b is 119 prompts, one short, and the structural complexity (27 regex scripts, 1.1 MB tavern_helper subtree) may matter more than the count. But the plan names 120+ explicitly as the stress tier, and a gate that claims it while testing 105 or 119 is the exact class M0 exists to find.

hypotheses.title: Nested/recursive world books are absent from the browser journey
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE: the fixture does not carry a character book or a recursive entry
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Stage a V3 card with data.character_book (one constant, one secondary-keys entry, one regex key) and a global book with recursion depth 2; assert the character-book marker, the recursive-trigger marker and the slot ORDER in the armed request, and assert the recursive marker disappears in the control turn.
hypotheses.counterargument: The world-info slot work (Q16/Q17, the two world-info gates) proves placement and activation for global books, and the card-a derivation carries 490 character-book entries that the asset/preset lanes read. But no gate asserts that a character-book or recursive entry reaches the provider wire in the combination session.

hypotheses.title: 10 of 13 same-SHA gates upload claims the release verifier never reads, and the extension-compat artifact has no root head SHA
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE: reading the publish-time table shows '-' in the artifact/evidence columns for those gates
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: For each gate that already writes a verdict document (whole-session comparison, combination-journey comparison, helper-state comparison, worldinfo comparison, extension-compat summary), add release-evidence.json with kind/headSha/pinnedSha and a requiredEvidence rail; start with the two that already compute teeth results.
hypotheses.counterargument: The manifest records this as intentional: a gate may be judged by its own conclusion, and each workflow's own terminal step is the claim. The plan's section 8 asks for artifact-level embedded evidence, so the gap is against the plan, not against alpha.15's stated design.

hypotheses.title: The browser gates fetch pinned extensions from github.com at gate time; the seed path exists but no workflow populates it
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE without network: the code path is only taken when no seed root is set
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Set GOTAVERN_EXTENSION_SEED_ROOT from a cached seed checkout in the combination/browser workflows, then assert every install result says source='seed' rather than source='remote' (the field already exists).
hypotheses.counterargument: The fetch is a git clone pinned to a 40-hex commit, so the content is immutable and no provider egress occurs; the origin is frozen afterwards and the revision is asserted. The risk is availability and gate flakiness, not correctness.

hypotheses.title: Committed browser evidence can be stale while the release gate is green
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE: any green run with stale>0 in the freshness report demonstrates it
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Make 'stale == 0' a required property for the release event, or move the freshness verdict into the uploaded evidence document and add a requiredEvidence rail; keep the report for push runs.
hypotheses.counterargument: The run re-records fresh artifacts into its own artifact, so the run's own evidence is current; only the COMMITTED artifact can be stale, and the docs say so. The scorecard rows that cite cancelled runs cite the completed steps by name, which is a documented and defensible practice.

hypotheses.title: The Docker gate can be green at the tag SHA without the publish path being exercised
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE: a default workflow_dispatch at the candidate SHA publishes nothing and still satisfies the gate
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Require the dispatch that satisfies the gate to carry a requiredEvidence document recording published+PulledBack=true (as the workflow already computes them), or move the Docker claim to the tag-push run and state that a dispatch proves build only.
hypotheses.counterargument: The tag push at the same commit does publish and pull back, so the alpha.15 evidence may be the tag-push run; but the manifest requires event=workflow_dispatch, which by construction cannot publish :latest and by default publishes nothing at all.

hypotheses.title: docs/perf-baseline.md says pprof capture is missing while the bench workflow captures it; server-process pprof is genuinely absent
hypotheses.reproducer: Run bench-profiles and observe cpu/mem/block/mutex pprof plus pprof-*-top.txt; the doc row says missing
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Correct the row to 'partial: in-process benchmark only; no server-process /debug/pprof', and keep the server-process gap as an explicit unmeasured row rather than implying it exists.
hypotheses.counterargument: The table's preface says exists = a committed artifact or gate; profiles are uploaded artifacts with 30-day retention, not committed, so 'partial' is the defensible state. 'missing' is still not the truth at HEAD.

hypotheses.title: 8-user concurrent-write performance has no harness
hypotheses.reproducer: NONE: E06's 8-user requirement has correctness coverage (two processes) and an in-flight concurrency mode on one route, but no per-user write load
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Add an 8-account concurrent settings/chats save mode to scripts/a15-bench-suite.mjs (fixturegen already has per-user trees): throughput, p50/p95/p99, CPU, lock waits, and byte assertions per user.
hypotheses.counterargument: Cross-user isolation and torn-write safety are already proven by the two-process test and the race job, so the load harness would measure cost, not correctness; the plan lists it as an environment, not a gate, and the workload table already calls it missing.

hypotheses.title: The whole-session self-test header undercounts its own mutations
hypotheses.reproducer: Read the run summary line: it reports applicable/applicable (for example 19/19) while the header says eleven and lists A-P only
hypotheses.reproducerPlan: Regenerate the header list from the MUTATIONS array (a computed footer, as A15-05 requires for the streaming selftest) so a stale count is red.
hypotheses.counterargument: It claims LESS than it computes, so it cannot produce a false green; it is the mirror image of the A15 false-greens and only costs a reader's trust.

questions: Did the alpha.15 release's 13 same-SHA runs actually use the full dispatch selection? The evidence table is in the published release body, not the tree, and the runs API does not expose dispatch inputs. Owner: Lead (release body) â€” and the durable fix is a selection marker plus a requiredEvidence rail, not a reading.

Is turn-1-world-info-three-slots-placed green on the current combination-journey pair? The selftest comment says the pinned leg's pre-boot world selection did not survive its boot. Deciding needs one browser run of combination-journey-probe.mjs on both subjects, which M0 forbids. Owner: Lane E in M1.

Which of the 20 pinned corpus extensions can contribute a deterministic, marker-bearing prompt-injection on the wire? The capability vocabulary says which classes exist, but the pinned source is not in this checkout. Owner: M1 scenario factory, against the pinned commits.
Is a build-tag-gated pprof listener (default off, --profile-addr, 127.0.0.1 only) acceptable as a product surface? That is a product decision, not an audit fact. Owner: Lead.

What is the real wall-clock cost of the first E03+E04 combined scenario? The current five legs are ~5-7 min each per the workflow comment; 22 extension installs and a 120-prompt assembly add an unmeasured amount. Only a run decides it.
